subject.title: [Bug] Agent automatically executes config commands from example code without user confirmation

question: Should model-initiated OpenClaw self-management commands such as config writes, model-default changes, gateway restarts, updates, and uninstall commands require explicit user confirmation even when host exec is otherwise configured as full/off?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but changing this behavior alters the security boundary and may affect operators who intentionally rely on full/off automation.

options.title: Require confirmation for self-management commands
options.body: Add a deterministic guarded class for OpenClaw config, model, gateway lifecycle, update, and uninstall commands while preserving full/off for ordinary trusted host exec.

options.title: Fold into the broader confirmation gate
options.body: Keep this issue open as a concrete scenario and wait for the response-level tool confirmation design at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/23451 before changing exec behavior.

options.title: Keep full/off unchanged
options.body: Document that operators must opt into stricter exec approvals or sandboxing and accept that raw exec can run these commands without an extra OpenClaw self-management prompt.

recommendation.title: Require confirmation for self-management commands
recommendation.body: Add a deterministic guarded class for OpenClaw config, model, gateway lifecycle, update, and uninstall commands while preserving full/off for ordinary trusted host exec.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, exec policy, and the agent-core tool execution loop, and current history routes the active lines through this area.
